To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) observers who are told that the target person has a facial scar are more likely than other observers to focus on nonverbal behavior and to segment the behavior stream into more breakpoints; and (2) observers who are instructed to focus on non-verbal behavior segment the behavior stream of a person with a facial scar more frequently than observers who are told to focus on verbal behavior.
the facial scar set led observers to attend to the nonverbal behavior of the stimulus person, and this led to the perception of more breakpoints in the stimulus tape than the allergy set.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the perceptual and cognitive processes involved in the interpretation of social interaction, and in particular with the role of social stereotypes in these processes.
the perception of social interaction and the influence of social stereotypes upon the perception process.
the effects of a social stimulus on observers' attention to the stimulus and the effects of observers' attention on their perception of the stimulus.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the facial scar set produced more segmentation than the allergy set.
facial scars are not the only factor that can influence the perception of social interaction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the facial scar set produced an increased focus on nonverbal cues and that this was reflected in a more detailed analysis of the stimulus behavior stream.
the facially scarred person's behavior was perceived as more complex, more ambiguous, and less meaningful than the behavior of the other three target persons.
the perception of social interaction is affected by the observer's belief about the physical condition of the target person.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the perception of social interaction is influenced by the observer’s beliefs about the target’s physical state and the type of behavior that the observer attends to.
the way in which we interpret the behavior of others is affected by our beliefs about them.
the way we think about others affects how we attend to and interpret their behavior.
